coverage_note: Transcripts/presentations available ONLY for FY2026 (4 quarters: Q1 08-Aug-25, Q2 07-Nov-25, Q3 30-Jan-26, Q4 30-Apr-26). No transcripts exist for FY2021-FY2025; all pre-FY2026 management-signalling context is limited to AR MD&A narrative (not separately re-extracted here). Credibility scoring below is therefore capped at 'medium' confidence even where hit-rate looks clean, because the track record is a single fiscal year (4 data points) observed by the same reporting management team, not a multi-year pattern. This cap is stated per family below, not re-derived.

executive_read.tone_verdict: Bullish / self-confident, delivered against a backdrop of a commodity-price headwind and one material operational slippage — management leans on volume and cost-efficiency achievement to talk past a realization miss.

tone_evidence.quote: Taking very challenging target this year 10% higher targets all areas. First quarter achieved all targets. Very sure achieving targets. End of year financials very good.
tone_evidence.speaker: CMD Brijendra Pratap Singh

tone_evidence.quote: This year, we have done best ever physical performance in all the areas, bauxite excavation, alumina hydrate production, calcined alumina production, metal production.
tone_evidence.speaker: CMD

tone_evidence.quote: There is growth of 33% in the revenue and the PAT has registered growth of 77% against the corresponding quarter last year.
tone_evidence.speaker: DGM (Mechanical)

top_2_drivers_their_framing: Volume growth across bauxite/alumina/metal/power — repeatedly cited as 'best ever' / record production and sales, used to offset a ~36% YoY alumina price decline ($580 to $370/t FY25 to FY26, QT-Q4-006).

Cost/techno-economic efficiency — caustic soda consumption improvement (121 kg/t to 99 kg/t 9M FY26, GD-Q3-014), captive coal ramp to 4 MTpa displacing costlier e-auction/linkage coal and grid power (GD-Q2-026 to GD-Q2-030), employee cost ratio decline via retirements (GD-Q2-032, GD-Q3-016).
top_2_risks_their_framing: Alumina price/oversupply — management explicitly attributes the realization decline to Indonesian refinery ramp-up and a compressed alumina-to-LME premium (15-17% to 11-11.5%, QT-Q4-006/GD-Q4-035), and (Q3) to Middle East geopolitical disruption to shipping.

5th-stream refinery execution slip — management itself flagged the commissioning date moved from Sept 2025 to June 2026 (GD-Q2-001 notes: 'Revised from September 2025... 80% physical completion') and the FY26 in-year volume contribution cut from 500KT to 300KT (GD-Q3-037, explicitly labelled a revision by the company).

rows.what_management_said: FY26 total alumina sales guided 12.5-12.8 lakh tons (Q1, GD-Q1-013); revised to 12-12.5 lakh tons (Q2, GD-Q2-014); Q3 guided 1250-1300 KT (GD-Q3-001).
rows.numeric_check_vs_facts: FY26 actual per Q4 call: export 13.09 lakh ton + domestic 1.37 lakh ton = 14.46 lakh ton total (QT-Q4-1011/quotes_TR_2026-04-30). Actual came in ABOVE every quarterly guide issued during the year by 13-20%.
rows.external_corroboration: pending research — no independent alumina volume tracker in file set
rows.implication: Volume guidance was systematically conservative/beaten, not missed — opposite failure mode from the refinery timeline. Feeds estimates-builder as a credible base but note the beat direction (upside bias, not precision).

rows.what_management_said: FY26 metal production guided 470K tons vs 450-460K rated capacity (Q2, GD-Q2-025; Q3 GD-Q3-009 refined to 470-472KT).
rows.numeric_check_vs_facts: Actual FY26 metal production 4.71 lakh tons (471KT) per Q4 (QT-Q4-002/context: 'cast metal production around 2.61% growth'; GD-Q4-003 states FY26 peak 4.71 lakh tons, FY27 target 4.73 lakh tons).
rows.implication: Near-exact hit (471 actual vs 470 guided) — best-scoring guide in the ledger.

rows.what_management_said: Caustic soda consumption guided 'sustainable' at 96 kg/ton (Q2, GD-Q2-033); Q3 reports 99 kg/ton 9M actual with Rs.129cr savings vs 121 kg/ton prior year (GD-Q3-014).
rows.numeric_check_vs_facts: 99 kg/ton 9M actual vs 96 kg/ton guided — modest miss (+3%) but directionally consistent and well ahead of prior year base.
rows.implication: Credible, delivered cost lever; small guide/actual gap not material.

rows.what_management_said: Q4 cost of production guided 'slightly higher' (GD-Q3-008) due to CP coke +Rs.7-8K/t and caustic soda tender increase, offset by efficiency.
rows.numeric_check_vs_facts: Q4 actual alumina cost Rs.20,000-22,000/t and metal cost Rs.155,000-160,000/t (GD-Q4-024, GD-Q4-025) — consistent with the directional 'slightly higher' guide; no hard miss identifiable from records provided.
rows.implication: Directional guides (non-numeric) are hard to score precisely but have not been contradicted.

rows.what_management_said: Alumina export/spot mix targeted at 80% spot/20% long-term (Q1, GD-Q1-014); Q2 describes a target 50/50 term-spot mix (GD-Q2-024, flagged 'refusal_Q2_contract_mix' quote ref — evasive answer candidate).
rows.numeric_check_vs_facts: Internal inconsistency: Q1 guide (80/20 spot-heavy) and Q2 guide (50/50 target) describe different desired mixes five months apart without an explicit reconciliation in the record set. By Q4, management states 'no long term alumina contracts... due to low pricing environment' (GD-Q4-036) — a third position.
rows.implication: Contradiction — see Section: Contradictions #2. Mix strategy has moved three times in one year, tracking price weakness rather than a stated strategy being executed to plan.

rows.what_management_said: Employee cost guided to decline from 18% of total cost (Q2, GD-Q2-031) to 15-16% by FY27 (GD-Q2-032) via retirements; Q3 guides Rs.70-100cr FY26 full-year reduction from 200-250 senior superannuations (GD-Q3-016).
rows.numeric_check_vs_facts: Q4 confirms stable headcount ~4,880 with ~250 retirements offset by 5th-stream recruitment (GD-Q4-038) — consistent with the guided mechanism; too early (only 2 quarters of data since the Nov-25 guide) to score hit/miss on the 15-16% FY27 target.
rows.implication: Plausible mechanical guide (retirement-driven), not yet verifiable — flag to re-run when FY27 transcripts land.

rows.what_management_said: Rs.2.50/share final dividend recommended by Board (Q1, GD-Q1-029).
rows.numeric_check_vs_facts: Stated as Board-recommended, not yet a guide-vs-actual pair (dividends are declared, not guided-then-missed in the way a volume target is) — treated as a fact, not scored for credibility.
rows.implication: No corporate action (buyback/M&A/demerger) under management discussion in this record set beyond the smelter JV structuring (see capex section) and the Neyveli Lignite 50-50 power JV (GD-Q4-027) — reasoned view in Section 4 below.

rows.what_management_said: Cash balance projected to exceed Rs.20,000cr by FY26-end (Q2, GD-Q2-012) from Rs.7,900cr as of Sept-2025; smelter capex external funding need Rs.5,000-6,000cr in EPC mode (vs none in JV mode) for FY28-29 (GD-Q2-013).
rows.numeric_check_vs_facts: No FY26-end cash actual is available in the record set provided (FY2026 AR not yet published per manifest gap). Cannot score — flagged as an open question for the next run once FY26 AR lands.
rows.implication: Debt-funded capex is not indicated; company signals self-funding via internal cash generation for the near-term capex plan, funding gap only appears in an EPC (non-JV) structuring scenario for the smelter — a scenario management appears to be steering away from (JV with Neyveli Lignite for power, GD-Q4-027).

rows.what_management_said: FY26 total capex guided Rs.1,700cr (Q3, GD-Q3-017).
rows.numeric_check_vs_facts: FY26 actual capex ~Rs.2,000cr (QT-Q4 context 'FY2026 capex actual Rs. 2000 cr') to Rs.2,100cr (Director Finance: 'Our target was Rs.1,700 crores, but we have exceeded by almost Rs.400 crores more' — implying ~Rs.2,100cr). Overrun of ~Rs.300-400cr, i.e. ~18-24% above guide.
rows.implication: Capex guide missed on the low side (spent more than guided) — for a PSU this typically reads as accelerated project execution rather than cost overrun in the pejorative sense (management frames it as pulling spend forward), but it is a quantified guidance miss and is scored as such in the ledger.

rows.what_management_said: 5th-stream refinery commissioning: Q1 guided June 2026 (already itself a revision from an original Sept-2025 plan referenced only in Q2's own framing, GD-Q2-001 notes). Confirmed June 2026 through Q2/Q3/Q4.
rows.numeric_check_vs_facts: Consistent June-2026 guide held across 3 consecutive quarters (Q2, Q3, Q4) after the initial slip — this is the post-revision guide, and it has NOT slipped again as of the Q4 (Apr-2026) call, i.e. two quarters of stability since the reset.
rows.external_corroboration: pending research — no independent commissioning tracker
rows.implication: One material slip (pre-Q1 baseline to June 2026), then held. Credibility on this specific milestone is 'low' for the original baseline, 'medium' for the reset date given only 2 quarters of post-reset stability.

rows.what_management_said: FY26 in-year alumina volume contribution from the 5th stream: Q1/Q2 guided 5-6 lakh tons (GD-Q1-002) / 5 lakh tons for FY27 (GD-Q2-004) — for FY26 itself, no explicit FY26 (as opposed to FY27) production number was guided until Q3.
rows.numeric_check_vs_facts: Q3 (Jan-2026) explicitly revises: 'Previously guided 5 lakh KT for FY26 from new refinery, now more realistic 3 lakh KT' (GD-Q3-037) — a company-labelled revision, cutting the number by 40% roughly 3 months after the original figure was implied. Given the commissioning start itself is June 2026 (after FY26 ends, since NALCO's FY26 = Apr25-Mar26), this FY26 volume contribution figure is effectively zero to negligible and the whole framing appears to migrate to FY27 by Q4 (GD-Q4-002: 2 lakh tons incremental FY27).
rows.implication: See Contradiction #1 below — this is the headline signal-set item and the clearest instance of guidance drift needing explicit disclosure.

rows.numeric_check_vs_facts: Dates given across the four transcripts/PPTs: Q1 transcript 'FY2027-FY2030' (3-4yr from pre-project, GD-Q1-023); Q2 transcript 'December 2030' (GD-Q2-008); Q2 PPT 'Jun-2031' (GD-PQ2-006); Q3 transcript 'by end-2030 or early H1-2031' (GD-Q3-022); Q3 PPT 'August 2030' (GD-PQ3-004); Q4 transcript 'Dec 2030 - early 2031' (GD-Q4-013); Q4 PPT contains an INTERNAL inconsistency — 'Likely Commissioning Aug 2030 per slide, but revised to Jun 2031 in table' within the SAME document (GD-PQ4-003 conditionality field).
rows.implication: See Contradiction #3 — the target date has moved across at least 3 distinct points (Aug-2030 / Dec-2030 / Jun-2031) across documents, and the Q4 presentation contradicts itself. This is a directionally consistent 'late-2030 to mid-2031' window but the imprecision itself is a credibility signal for a project still in DPR/pre-tender stage.

rows.what_management_said: Alumina realization outlook: Q1 guided $400-450/t (GD-Q1-010) for 'coming quarters' off a Q1 actual of $416; Q2 guided H2 FY26 $320-340/t (GD-Q2-015) off a Q2 actual of $380 and then-current spot of $320; Q3 guided Q4 $310-320/t (GD-Q3-006).
rows.numeric_check_vs_facts: Q4 actual realization $348/t (GD-Q4-037 context: 'Q4 '25-'26 average realization was somewhere around 3,000/tons. Alumina, it is $348'). Actual $348 came in ABOVE the Q3 guide range of $310-320 (beat by ~9%), but well BELOW the Q1 guide range of $400-450 (miss by ~20-27%). FY25 to FY26 full-year average fell $580 to $370 (QT-Q4-006).
rows.external_corroboration: pending research — LME/AWP alumina index not independently pulled in this run
rows.implication: Price guidance decayed monotonically downward each quarter (450→340→320) as the market moved against the company, then the actual outcome beat only the most recently reset (most conservative) guide. This is a classic 'ratchet down, then clear the lowered bar' pattern — the ledger scores the family 'low' credibility on absolute level, 'medium' on most-recent-quarter precision.

rows.what_management_said: Aluminium/LME price outlook: Q2 guided H2 FY26 INR2,800-2,900/t (~USD equivalent, GD-Q2-016); Q3 guided Q4 $2,900-3,000 and FY27 $2,800-3,000 (GD-Q3-010, GD-Q3-011); Q4 guided FY27 $3,000-3,100 normalized ex-war-premium (GD-Q4-006), Q1 FY27 actual/near-term $3,500-3,600 (GD-Q4-007).
rows.numeric_check_vs_facts: Q4 FY26 actual realization ~$2,700-2,767/t per company commentary (quotes_TR_2026-04-30 context 'Q4 FY2026 aluminium realization $2767') vs Q3's own Q4 guide of $2,900-3,000 — a miss on the low side of roughly 5-7%, though within a reasonable band. FY27 guide of $3,000-3,100 'normalized' is explicitly hedged as contingent on war-premium unwind — an assumption not yet testable.
rows.implication: Metal price guide missed modestly to the downside for Q4 FY26 itself even as spot LME has since spiked on geopolitical premium — illustrates management guides on commodity price are directional color, not precision forecasts, consistent with the citation standard's caution on external-dependent claims.

guidance_ledger.history_one_line: Beat 3/3 verifiable full-year volume guides (FY26 alumina total sales actual 14.46 lakh tons vs successive guides of 12.5-12.8, then 12-12.5, then 12.5-13.0 lakh tons) — consistently conservative, never missed low.
guidance_ledger.credibility_rationale: Hit rate is high (>100% of guide achieved each time), which nominally scores 'high', but capped to 'medium' because: (a) single fiscal year of transcript history (per coverage_note), (b) the guide itself moved down mid-year (Q1 to Q2) before the beat, meaning part of the 'beat' is against an already-lowered bar, not the original one.
guidance_ledger.feeds_estimates_builder: Use FY26 actual (14.46 lakh tons) as the base; treat FY27 alumina volume guidance (25 lakh tons total, GD-Q4-001) as upside-biased per this history — a conservative haircut is not warranted given the beat pattern, but the 5th-stream incremental piece (2 lakh tons, GD-Q4-002) should be treated separately per the capex family below.

guidance_ledger.history_one_line: Met 1/1 verifiable full-year metal production guide almost exactly (470K guided vs 471K actual, <0.3% variance).
guidance_ledger.credibility: high (within-year), capped medium for track-record depth
guidance_ledger.credibility_rationale: Tightest hit in the ledger. Capped from 'high' only by the single-year data constraint stated in coverage_note, not by any miss.
guidance_ledger.feeds_estimates_builder: FY27 metal production guide of 4.73 lakh tons (GD-Q4-003) is a credible base-case input given this precision.

guidance_ledger.history_one_line: One material slip (implied Sept-2025 baseline to June-2026, a ~9-month push) surfaced and admitted by management in Q2; the reset June-2026 date then held stable across 3 subsequent quarters (Q2, Q3, Q4 all confirm June 2026).
guidance_ledger.credibility_rationale: A single slip on a headline capacity project is a material miss regardless of stability afterward. Per the guidance-analyst mandate this must not become an unquestioned base-case input — the post-reset date should carry an explicit execution-risk discount in the model until an actual June-2026 commissioning is confirmed (next data point needed: Q1 FY27 transcript, expected ~Aug-2026).
guidance_ledger.feeds_estimates_builder: Do NOT treat June-2026 as a high-confidence date for base case; carry a downside scenario with a further 1-2 quarter slip given the track record on this specific asset.

guidance_ledger.history_one_line: Guided FY26 contribution cut from an implied ~5 lakh tons (500KT) to 3 lakh tons (300KT) within the same fiscal year — a company-labelled 40% downward revision (GD-Q3-037) — then effectively deferred to FY27 (200KT incremental, GD-Q4-002) by year-end.
guidance_ledger.credibility_rationale: Explicit, management-acknowledged revision within a single fiscal year on a headline growth metric. This is the single clearest miss in the ledger and should NOT be used as a margin/volume tailwind in near-term (FY27 H1) base-case estimates without a haircut.
guidance_ledger.feeds_estimates_builder: Use the Q4 framing (2 lakh tons FY27 incremental, upside case 3-3.5 lakh tons if early commissioning per GD-Q4-002 note) as the base, but flag to estimates-builder that this same lever has already been cut once — apply a probability-weighted (not point) estimate.

guidance_ledger.history_one_line: Commissioning date has been stated as Aug-2030, Dec-2030, and Jun-2031 across different documents within the same 9-month window (including a self-contradictory PPT, GD-PQ4-003); combined capex estimate also moved from Rs.30,000cr (Q2) to Rs.23,000-24,000cr (Q4, on JV restructuring of the power plant).
guidance_ledger.credibility_rationale: Project is still pre-DPR/pre-tender as of Q4 FY26 (DPR targeted Aug-Sept 2026, GD-Q4-011) — every date and capex figure given so far is a planning estimate, not a delivered milestone, and the figures have not stabilized even directionally (three discrete dates, two discrete capex totals in under a year of disclosure).
guidance_ledger.feeds_estimates_builder: Treat 0.5 MTPA smelter capacity as a post-FY2030 scenario item only, excluded from the explicit forecast horizon (FY27-FY29) entirely; capex phasing (GD-Q4-016/017/018: FY27 Rs.1,800-2,000cr, FY28 Rs.4,000-5,000cr, FY29-30 Rs.8,000-10,000cr) should carry low confidence given the underlying project has no DPR yet.

guidance_ledger.history_one_line: Q1 guided a Feb-June 2026 window; Q2 transcript narrowed to June 2026 while the same quarter's PPT said May-2026; Q3 PPT restates May-2026. As of Q4 (Apr-2026) call, no confirmation of actual commissioning is present in the record set — status unresolved at period end.
guidance_ledger.credibility_rationale: Transcript-vs-PPT date mismatch within the same reporting quarter (Q2: June per call, May per deck) is an internal inconsistency, not just normal guidance narrowing. Combined with an MDO tender still 'ongoing'/'this month' as late as Nov-2025 for a claimed May-2026 commissioning, the timeline is tight and unverified.
guidance_ledger.feeds_estimates_builder: Do not assume Pottangi captive bauxite offset is live before Q1 FY27 close at the earliest; model a slip scenario given the tight tender-to-commissioning runway.

guidance_ledger.history_one_line: FY26 capex guided Rs.1,700cr (Q3, Jan-2026) vs actual ~Rs.2,000-2,100cr (Q4, Apr-2026) — missed (spent more) by ~Rs.300-400cr (~18-24%).
guidance_ledger.credibility_rationale: A capex overrun of this magnitude late in the year (guide given only one quarter before year-end) suggests either the Q3 guide undercounted committed spend or year-end catch-up/advance payments occurred. Not necessarily a red flag on its own (company frames it as accelerated execution) but is a quantified miss and should discount confidence in the FY27 capex guide (Rs.1,800-2,000cr, GD-Q3-018/GD-Q4-016) which has now been repeated unchanged across two quarters.
guidance_ledger.feeds_estimates_builder: Apply a modest upward bias (not haircut) to FY27 capex vs the stated Rs.1,800-2,000cr band, consistent with the FY26 pattern of exceeding near-term capex guides.

guidance_ledger.history_one_line: Guide ratcheted down each quarter ($400-450 to $320-340 to $310-320) tracking a falling spot market; Q4 actual ($348) beat only the most recently lowered guide, missing the original Q1 guide by ~20-27%.
guidance_ledger.credibility_rationale: This is a commodity price call, not an operational guide — management has limited control and the pattern (chase the market down, then narrowly beat the latest number) is the textbook signature of a low-credibility price guide. Per the module mandate, this must not become a base-case margin assumption without independent corroboration.
guidance_ledger.feeds_estimates_builder: Route to deep-research (industry/commodity) before using any of the FY27 alumina price points (GD-Q4-005: $300-310/t) as a base-case input — treat as company's own directional view only, cross-check against independent alumina index (e.g. Non-ferrous/AWP) in DR2.

guidance_ledger.history_one_line: Q3's own Q4 FY26 guide ($2,900-3,000) missed low vs actual (~$2,700-2,767); separately, the company's CY2026 LME average guide moved from $2,670 (Q2/Q3 PPT) to $3,125 (Q4 PPT) — a ~17% upward revision in one quarter, coinciding with a geopolitical price spike.
guidance_ledger.credibility_rationale: Same commodity-forecast caveat as alumina; the CY2026 average guide jumping 17% quarter-to-quarter shows the 'guidance' is essentially a restated market consensus/spot extrapolation, not an independent view with a track record of accuracy.
guidance_ledger.feeds_estimates_builder: Do not anchor FY27 LME assumptions to the company's own $3,000-3,100 'normalized' view (GD-Q4-006) without independent verification — this is explicitly a war-premium-adjustment guess. Route to DR2 (sector/commodity).

guidance_ledger.history_one_line: Guided 4 MTpa FY26 (from a 2.6-2.7 MT base) held consistently across all four quarters and appears to have been delivered (Q4 confirms captive coal production growth of 41.84% YoY, consistent with the ramp to ~4 MT).
guidance_ledger.credibility_rationale: Consistent guide, no revisions, YoY growth rate cited at Q4 (41.84%) is directionally consistent with a 2.6-2.7 MT to ~4 MT ramp (+~48-54%), a reasonably close match. Capped at 'medium-high' rather than 'high' only because an exact FY26 tonnage actual (vs the 4 MT guide) is not stated verbatim in the record set — inferred from the growth-rate quote, not a directly matched figure.
guidance_ledger.feeds_estimates_builder: FY27 captive coal guide of 4.8 MT (GD-Q4-008, subject to EC clearance for Utkal D&E blocks) can be used as base case with a footnote on the EC-clearance conditionality.

margin_bridge_achievability.bridge_described: Management's implicit margin bridge for FY27 rests on three levers: (1) volume growth (5th-stream ramp + Pottangi captive bauxite reducing purchased-bauxite cost), (2) cost efficiency (caustic soda, captive coal/power substitution, employee cost decline from retirements), (3) partial commodity price recovery (alumina and LME both assumed to firm from FY26 trough levels).

lever_scoring.basis: Same lever already cut once in-year (500KT to 300KT to effectively FY27-only, 200KT); commissioning date itself has one prior slip on record.
Transcript/PPT date mismatch (May vs June 2026) and late MDO tendering as of Nov-2025 for a claimed May-2026 start; no confirmed actual commissioning in the record set through Q4 FY26.

lever_scoring.lever: Cost efficiency (caustic soda, coal, employee cost)
lever_scoring.basis: This is the one lever with a clean, consistent, non-revised delivery track record across all four FY26 quarters (caustic soda 121→99 kg/t; coal captive ramp delivered; employee cost mechanically tied to scheduled retirements).

Price guidance has been the least reliable family in the ledger (ratcheted down each quarter on alumina; 17% one-quarter swing on the LME CY2026 view) — achievability of the assumed recovery is a market call, not a management-controlled lever.

margin_bridge_achievability.overall_achievability: Medium-Low — the only lever with a clean multi-quarter delivery record is cost efficiency; the two volume/capacity levers both carry an admitted in-year revision, and the price lever is explicitly outside management's control and has shown the largest guide-to-guide swings in the ledger.

customer_orderbook_concentration.note: NALCO sells alumina (export/domestic) and aluminium (LME-linked, largely domestic) as a commodity producer — no discrete 'customer' or 'orderbook' concentration metric of the kind used for order-book businesses is disclosed in the transcripts/PPTs reviewed. Closest analogues: alumina export/domestic sales split (Q4 FY26: 13.09 lakh ton export vs 1.37 lakh ton domestic, ~90.5%/9.5%) and the spot/term contract mix (contradictory across quarters, see Contradiction #2). No single-customer or top-N-customer disclosure found — flag as N/A for concentration red-flag scoring at this time, not a gap in extraction.

contradictions.claim: FY26 volume contribution from the 5th-stream alumina refinery
contradictions.description: Q1/Q2 guidance implied ~5 lakh tons (500KT) of FY26 alumina volume from the new refinery; Q3 (Jan-2026) explicitly revises this to 3 lakh tons (300KT), labelled by the company itself as a revision ('now more realistic 3 lakh KT'); by Q4 the framing has shifted entirely to FY27 (2 lakh tons incremental). Net effect: the originally implied FY26 contribution appears to have been ~zero to negligible once the June-2026 commissioning date (itself a slip from an implied Sept-2025 baseline) is applied to a Apr-Mar fiscal year.

contradictions.claim: Desired alumina export contract mix (spot vs term/long-term)
contradictions.description: Q1 states an 80% spot / 20% long-term target mix, framed as a deliberate shift 'due to pricing.' Q2 states a target of 50% term contracts / 50% spot (opposite direction) with the underlying quote itself flagged 'refusal_Q2_contract_mix' (evasive-answer candidate) in the source record. Q4 then states no long-term contracts are being written at all ('spot_only') due to the low-price environment. Three distinct, mutually inconsistent positions on the same strategic variable within one fiscal year.

Commissioning date stated variously as December 2030 (Q2 transcript), June 2031 (Q2 PPT), August 2030 (Q3 PPT), 'end-2030 or early H1-2031' (Q3/Q4 transcripts), and the Q4 PPT itself contains both August-2030 (slide) and June-2031 (table) without reconciliation — an internal document inconsistency, not just a cross-quarter drift.

contradictions.claim: Combined smelter + power plant capex estimate
contradictions.description: Q2 guides a combined Rs.30,000cr (smelter Rs.17-20k cr + power Rs.10-11k cr). Q4 restates as Rs.23,000-24,000cr total (smelter Rs.17-18k cr + NALCO's 50% share of a Rs.12k cr power JV with Neyveli Lignite, i.e. Rs.6k cr net to NALCO) — management attributes the reduction to the JV structuring decision, which is a reasonable explanation, but the headline combined number moved by ~20-23% between quarters on a project still pre-DPR.
contradictions.note: Not flagged as a red-flag candidate because management provides an internally consistent structural reason (JV cost-sharing) for the change, unlike F-GUI-01/03 which show no reconciling explanation.

contradictions.description: Q2 transcript states June 2026; the same quarter's PPT states May 2026 for the identical milestone — a same-quarter, same-document-set mismatch between the verbal call and the accompanying deck.

FY26 metal production actual 4.71 lakh ton vs guided 4.70 lakh ton (hit)
FY26 capex actual ~Rs.2,000-2,100cr vs guided Rs.1,700cr (miss, overrun ~18-24%)
Q4 FY26 alumina realization actual $348/t vs Q3 guide $310-320/t (beat) vs Q1 guide $400-450/t (miss)
Q4 FY26 aluminium realization actual ~$2,700-2,767/t vs Q3 guide $2,900-3,000/t (miss, low side ~5-7%)
